```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins) # load AFTER tidyverse; masks datasets::penguins on R >= 4.5
```

## Introduction and data source

This report compares bill size and body mass of three penguin species
(Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo) on three islands in the Palmer Archipelago,
Antarctica. Dr Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station Long Term Ecological
Research programme collected the data from 2007 to 2009. We use the copy in
the `palmerpenguins` R package (Horst, Hill and Gorman, 2020), which has
`r nrow(penguins)` rows and `r ncol(penguins)` columns.
The data are released under a CC0 licence (Horst, Hill and Gorman, 2020;
Gorman, Williams and Fraser, 2014).

## Data cleaning

```{r}
#| label: clean

penguins_clean <- penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |>
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000)
```

We removed the `r nrow(penguins) - nrow(penguins_clean)` rows with missing
`sex`. These include the `r sum(is.na(penguins$body_mass_g))` rows with no body
measurements at all. The cleaned
data have `r nrow(penguins_clean)` rows. We added body mass in kilograms
(`body_mass_kg`).

## Summary tables

```{r}
#| label: tbl-species
#| tbl-cap: "Number of penguins, mean and standard deviation of bill length (mm), flipper length (mm) and body mass (g) by species."

species_summary <- penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    bill_length_mean = mean(bill_length_mm),
    bill_length_sd = sd(bill_length_mm),
    flipper_length_mean = mean(flipper_length_mm),
    flipper_length_sd = sd(flipper_length_mm),
    body_mass_mean = mean(body_mass_g),
    body_mass_sd = sd(body_mass_g),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(species_summary, digits = 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-island-sex
#| tbl-cap: "Number of penguins of each species by island and by sex."

island_counts <- penguins_clean |>
  count(species, island) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = island, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

sex_counts <- penguins_clean |>
  count(species, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n)

knitr::kable(left_join(island_counts, sex_counts, by = "species"))
```

Adelie penguins live on all three islands. Chinstrap penguins appear only
on Dream and Gentoo penguins only on Biscoe, so island and species are
partly confounded.

## Figures

```{r}
#| label: fig-bill
#| fig-cap: "Bill depth against bill length, with a straight-line fit for each species."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

p_bill <- ggplot(
  penguins_clean,
  aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, colour = species)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)", colour = "Species") +
  theme_minimal()

p_bill
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mass
#| fig-cap: "Body mass by species, split by sex. Boxes show the median and quartiles; points show individual penguins."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

p_mass <- ggplot(penguins_clean, aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~sex) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Body mass (g)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_mass
```

## Simple comparison

```{r}
#| label: slopes

overall_slope <- coef(lm(bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins_clean))[[2]]

species_slopes <- penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(slope = coef(lm(bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm))[2])

knitr::kable(species_slopes, digits = 3)
```

Across all penguins, the fitted slope is `r round(overall_slope, 3)` mm of
bill depth per millimetre of bill length: longer bills look *shallower*.
Within every species the slope is *positive* (table above and
@fig-bill). The overall trend is an example of Simpson's paradox: Gentoo
penguins have long but shallow bills, and pooling the species hides the
relationship inside each one. Species must be part of any model of bill shape.

```{r}
#| label: mass-model

mass_model <- lm(body_mass_g ~ species, data = penguins_clean)
summary(mass_model)
```

Adelie is the reference species, so the intercept
(`r round(coef(mass_model)[[1]])` g) is the mean Adelie body mass.
Gentoo penguins are on average `r round(coef(mass_model)[["speciesGentoo"]])` g
heavier than Adelie penguins. The Chinstrap difference
(`r round(coef(mass_model)[["speciesChinstrap"]])` g) is small compared with
its standard error. Species explains
`r round(100 * summary(mass_model)$r.squared)`% of the variation in body mass.

## Limitations

- The data are observational, so the comparisons describe differences and do
  not show causes.
- Species and island are partly confounded (Chinstrap only on Dream, Gentoo
  only on Biscoe), so we cannot separate species effects from island effects.
- The model of body mass ignores sex, although males are heavier in every
  species (@fig-mass). We did not formally check the model's assumptions
  (normality of residuals, equal variance); we only inspected plots of the
  raw data.
- We removed `r nrow(penguins) - nrow(penguins_clean)` rows with missing `sex` and did not
  investigate why they were missing.
- We include only methods we can explain. We did not use any analysis an AI
  assistant suggested that we could not interpret ourselves.
